data.hypothesis: A flattened, statically scheduled pixel loop should expose enough independent work while preserving contiguous pixel writes and avoiding per-iteration scheduler overhead. A direct serial path at one requested thread avoids OpenMP team overhead in the 1-core case. Pixel-keyed SplitMix64 streams should make the same uniform sequence recur for a given seed and pixel regardless of scheduling or thread count.
data.notes: This proposal has not been run locally. The supplied baseline-e1 is correct and reports three timings averaging 3.4961 s, but those observations do not provide candidate timings per official configuration. Correctness and repeated performance measurements, including the 1-thread case, remain for controller evaluation.
transformations: Replace shared drand48 state with a SplitMix64 stream initialized from the input seed and linear pixel index; each pixel advances only its local stream.
Flatten the image to a pixel-index loop with static OpenMP scheduling and num_threads bounded by the requested thread count; execute serially when one thread is requested.
Preserve the primary-ray and ambient-ray loops, intersection geometry, and per-pixel accumulation order; each iteration writes only its own RGB triplet.
